reviews.content:
This book was a true blessing to us. While our daughter was a pretty good newborn (didn't cry much at all), we quickly got frustrated with her being up until 10. . . 10:30. . . 11. . . or even midnight! We felt like we didn't have a life because, well, we didn't. That's what prompted us to buy the book.

The biggest point that changed our life here was Elizabeth saying that babies should be put to sleep for the night at 7-7:30. I honestly didn't believe it and she addressed that in the book. . . saying people would be scared that doing that would mean the baby would be awake at 3am. That was us.

We were thinking our daughter was napping when she fell asleep in the early evening because she'd usually wake up in ~30-45 minutes, staying up until much later. It was us who were causing the problem, since we'd play with her and have her active after she'd had that ""nap"". So, we were astonished when we put her down for the night for the first time at 7-7:30 and she didn't fully wake again until 7 the next morning (just a few brief nighttime wake-ups. . . which we're working on). We also established a bedtime routine, as Elizabeth suggests. Again, astonished that babies take these cues and know what they mean after a short number of days. She completely winds down after her bath and is usually nearly asleep when I read her stories.

What I like best about this book is that Elizabeth is honest and matter-of-fact. Babies are human and that means change will take some time. . . and sometimes things will mess with the changes you make (like teething that hit us in the 5th and 6th month big-time). You just have to re-group and stay committed, knowing that you're doing what's best for your baby. . . and you! Elizabeth's encouragement to persevere is just what you need to hear.

Now, my husband and I have time together -- alone -- in the evenings. And we're getting much more sleep, which makes us better parents and better people out in the world. :-)

I'm now reading the No-Cry Nap Solution. . . although naps are pretty good right now. Still, I figure if I get even a few tips to make things better, all the better for us and our baby.
reviews.title: A very helpful book

reviews.content:
I cannot say enough great things about this book. I stumbled upon it at the bookstore a few weeks back. I was looking for anything to help me get out of the fog I was walking around in from lack of sleep. I have a 10 month old daughter who is ""determined, stubborn, and strong willed"". This is a quote from her pediatrician. We got to the point where she would wake up 8 to 10 times a night wanting to nurse and if she didn't she would SCREAM. I mean really scream!!!! She hated her crib and would get so upset that she would start hyperventilating. 

The cover with the lovely sleeping baby pulled me in and by the first paragraph I was enthralled. What made me like this book so much was the easy, gentle, open suggestions for each UNIQUE family. We were seriously sleep deprived and I was crying at the drop of a hat. Pantley's book gave me suggestions for EVERY situation. She covered the breastfeeder, the bottle feeder, co-sleeping, crib sleeping etc. At first my husband rolled his eyes at me because he said NOTHING would work. . she was just stubborn. He is now Pantley's second biggest fan! (behind me of course). 

I am so delighted and amazed to say that our little girl is now sleeping through the night most nights. We made a plan, STUCK TO IT, and by the 3rd night she only woken up twice, AND she put herself back to sleep once!!! I can honestly tell you that the thought and love in which the author puts into this book makes you truly feel like you will make it through. . . and then if you use the book correctly, YOU DO! I am going on the 3rd night of sleeping through the night and it's only been 3 weeks since we started this. Since the 3rd night we've only had 2 night wakings max and we don't ever have to take her out of the crib if we have to intervene. Using Pantley's suggestions she now loves her crib! It's wonderful! 

I was desperate and at the end of my rope. This book was a blessing! I recommend it to everyone.
reviews.title: Best book for Sleep Deprived Moms!

reviews.content:
After almost 1 year of sleep deprivation, this book has truly changed the night-time dynamics in our household and has allowed both my husband and I to become fully functional adults again. Our child-raising beliefs did not contemplate the option of a ""let-the-baby-cry-it-out"" method. But we still aspired to get a decent night of sleep. The ""No Cry Sleep Solution"" really worked for us. 

First of all, it provided us with background information about what a baby's sleep cycle is truly like, ridding us of unreasonable expectations and allowing us to understand our baby better. Then it went on to provide very concrete and specific tools, along with the explanation of why they are likely to work. Because every baby is different, a number of different alternatives are offered. And no, these methods are not magical - they all require the involvement and engagement of the parents or care takers. But we have found that this effort was minimal compared to the bleak outlook of not sleeping through the night for a very, very long time. 

In our case, it took us about 6 weeks for our baby to go from waking up 4-6 times a night to sleeping through the night most of the time. Of those 6 weeks, only the first two were somewhat challenging as our baby adapted to these new methods, but no more challenging than it was trying to run our lives day in and day out in a constant state of sleep deprivation. The ""final"" 4 weeks were easier and easier, as our baby showed a gradual improvement (i. e. reduction) in her night time awakenings. For example, the last two weeks were almost exclusively one awakening per night (of a 12-hour period), until now, in which she has had many nights of sleeping 12 hours all the way through.

Additionally, one of the tools proposed, the pre-bedtime routine, is not only an essential part of getting your baby to sleep through the night but also has become a very important bonding moment and highly enjoyable for all of us.

Elizabeth Pantley shares her experience of being the mother of 4 with a lot of clarity, insight and an immense amount of compassion. We highly recommend this book.
reviews.title: Very happy to have come across this book

reviews.content: This book was an absolute family-saver. I stumbled on it in my local library when my daughter was about 8 months old (and was still waking SEVERAL times each night). She is naturally a sensitive child and a bit petite, so there was no way I had the heart to deny her to nurse if she was hungry or comfort when she woke up screaming. Within a few weeks of picking up the book, our daughter was up to sleeping 10+ hours each night with an occasional mid-night feeding. She now at 14 months sleeps 12 hours straight, usually even through teething and illness, and wakes up cheerful and plays quietly in her crib until someone comes to get her. The book is not a one-size fits all solution, it's so much better than that. First, Elizabeth explains the basics of sleep-like how much sleep your child really needs, what the phases of sleep look and sound like and reading your child's sleepy signals. She believes there is no right or wrong way answer sleep issues, but instead gives lots of loving suggestions to create positive associations with sleep and find the combination that works best for you.
reviews.title: THE BEST in Sleep Solutions

reviews.content: My son was sleeping for 30 minutes at a time and I was at my wits-end! I don't believe in cry it out, so that was not an option, but I needed sleep! A good friend recommended this book and I immediately bought it. I LOVE IT!!! Elizabeth Pantley shares strategies for families that co-sleep, crib sleep, breastfeed or bottle feed. Her strategies work and are very gentle, just what I was looking for! I have used this with 2 of my children so far, and am re-reading the book now to use with my new baby. You will NOT be sorry if you buy this book. It works, it is fabulous!

reviews.content: This is a wonderful book and was a life saver for my little guy and our family. After months of frustrating nights and waking every hour I needed a solution that didn't include leaving him to cry. Our local public health nurse recommended The no cry sleep solution. This book was a real eye opener on how I needed to help my little one sleep. We went from hourly night wakings and feedings down to sleeping through the night with an occasional wake up. No tears, no fuss. At the end of our evening routine he puts himself to sleep after chatting to himself and playing with his ""LOVEY"". He went from short 20 mintue naps to having two 1. 5-2 hour naps a day. It didn't happen overnight but we saw a HUGE difference after just one week. In one week we went from about 10 wake ups a night down to about 3 and it got better and better! It's an easy read and applies to breastfeeding or bottlefeeding moms! It's a must read for anyone with a baby. In fact, I wish I'd read it when I was pregnant!!!!
